tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.

schema.description:

   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@

tools.name: PushNotification
tools.description:
This tool sends a desktop notification in the user's terminal. If Remote Control is connected, it also pushes to their phone. Either way, it pulls their attention from whatever they're doing — a meeting, another task, dinner — to this session. That's the cost. The benefit is they learn something now that they'd want to know now: a long task finished while they were away, a build is ready, you've hit something that needs their decision before you can continue.

Because a notification they didn't need is annoying in a way that accumulates, err toward not sending one. Don't notify for routine progress, or to announce you've answered something they asked seconds ago and are clearly still watching, or when a quick task completes. Notify when there's a real chance they've walked away and there's something worth coming back for — or when they've explicitly asked you to notify them.

Keep the message under 200 characters, one line, no markdown. Lead with what they'd act on — "build failed: 2 auth tests" tells them more than "task done" and more than a status dump.

When the user is actively at the terminal, your output already reaches them — a notification on top of it would be a duplicate, so the tool skips it and says so. A "not sent" result is expected and only ever about this one notification: it was redundant, turned off, or had nowhere to go.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

### 2. The "Gameplay Tab" Component (`VinylPlayer.tsx`)

#### How It Works
1. **Filter Initialization**:
   On mount, `VinylPlayer` queries Tier 5 (`_5_config.db`) via `getFilterConfig` to retrieve the user's saved filter settings (`selectedChannel`, `excludedChannels`, `hazardCap`).
2. **Track Pool Sampling**:
   `loadData()` requests sampled tracks from `_1_static.db` via `fetchSampledTracks()`, taking active include channels, exclude channels, hazard cap, and blocked track IDs into account. It also loads `channelList`, `customPlaylists`, and `channelMetaMap`.
3. **Roulette Track Selection**:
   Tracks are picked via an $O(N)$ weighted roulette selection algorithm (`selectWeightedTrack`), where track weight is inversely proportional to play count ($w = \frac{1}{\text{played} + 1}$), prioritizing less-frequently played songs.
4. **Buffer Replenishment**:
   The player maintains up to 50 tracks in memory (`playlist`). When the remaining buffer drops below 15 tracks, `replenishBufferIfNeeded()` automatically samples additional songs in the background.
5. **Playback and Watchdog**:

   * **Ended**: When a track finishes, if `autoplay` is enabled, it automatically logs the track with the default or selected rating to Tier 2 and advances to the next song.
   * **Errors**: If YouTube error codes (100, 101, 150) fire, the track is buffered to `unavailable_videos.jsonl` and auto-advances.

#### What Is Displayed
* **Telemetry Header**:
  * **Include Selector**: Dropdown to stream All Playlists (`ALL`), a specific Custom Playlist (`CUSTOM:<id>`), curated groups (`STATUS:approved`, `STATUS:cleaning`, `STATUS:raw`), or an individual channel.
  * **Live Hazard Drag Badge**: Shows how many 3.0 songs need removal to gain +0.01 average hazard.
  * **Exclude Dropdown Popover**: Multi-select interface to exclude custom playlists or individual channels.
  * **Hazard Cap Selector**: Filter by hazard range (7+, 6+, 3.2 to <6.0, <4.0, <3.2, All).
  * **Metrics Badges**: Pool song count, session rated count, earned discs, offline outbox count, auto-sync batch counter (`X/15`), and buffer gauge bar.
* **Left Column (Player Viewport)**:
  * Buffer index and total pool size (`TRACK X / Y • Z in Pool`).
  * Current track title (`currentTrack.title`).
  * Current track metadata: Channel origin (`currentTrack.channel`), ID, play count, hazard badge, and pick chance percentage.
  * 16:9 YouTube video player container (`#vinyl-yt-player`).
* **Right Column (Harmonic Rating Deck)**:
  * Pinned Rating Latch (`Pin` button to lock ratings/ranks across tracks).
  * Target toggle: "Single Song" (`'track'`) vs "All in Channel" (`'channel'`).
  * Quick action row: Cancel (3+), Spin (Skip), and Pass/Log button.
  * Hazard Rank staging buttons: 3 (Base), 4 (Solid), 5 (Prime), 6 (Awaken), 7 (Crown).
  * Score Tier buttons: 3+, 4+, 5+, 6+, 7+.
  * Timeblock Arc tags: Arc Zero through Arc 04.
  * Dual Block buttons: "Block & Skip Now" (immediate deletion) and "Block on Track End".

#### Where Current Playing Song and Playlist State Comes From
* **Current Song**:
  Derived from local component state: `currentTrack = playlist[currentIndex]`.
  * `playlist`: Array of `PlaylistItem` loaded from `fetchSampledTracks()`.
  * `currentIndex`: Active index in `playlist`.
  * The origin playlist / channel of the playing song is given by `currentTrack.channel` (and `currentTrack.channel_id`).
* **Current Playing Playlist / Stream Source**:
  * Tracked by `selectedChannel` in `VinylPlayer.tsx` (e.g. `'ALL'`, `'CUSTOM:<id>'`, or a channel name).
  * When navigating from the Playlists tab, `queuedPlaylistForGameplay` in `useVinylStore` seeds `selectedChannel`.
  * Saved to Tier 5 backend database (`_5_config.db`) via `saveFilterConfig()`.

### 3. How Playlists Are Managed, Stored, and Structured

There are two distinct playlist concepts in the architecture:

#### A. The Active Playing Playlist (Stream Filter)
* **What it is**: The active playback filter that determines which tracks are sampled into the Gameplay buffer.
* **State**: Local React state `selectedChannel` in `VinylPlayer.tsx`.
* **Cross-Tab Transfer**: `useVinylStore.queuedPlaylistForGameplay`.
* **Persistence**: Persisted to SQLite database `backend/data/projects/music_app/app_data/_5_config.db` in table `tier_5_data` under the key `'filter_settings'`.

#### B. The Custom Playlist (Channel Federation)
* **What it is**: A user-defined thematic collection that groups multiple music channels / origin playlists together.
* **Data Structure (`types.ts`)**:
  ```ts
  export interface CustomPlaylist {
    id: string;                      // e.g. "pl_1712900000000_abcde"
    name: string;                    // e.g. "Epic Battle Orchestral"
    emoji: string;                   // e.g. "⚔️"
    description?: string;
    channels: string[];              // Array of channel / origin playlist names
    compatible_timeblocks?: string[]; // e.g. ["Arc 02 ~ Battle Phase - Racheal"]
    created_at: string;              // ISO timestamp
    updated_at: string;              // ISO timestamp
  }
  ```
* **Key Architectural Invariant**:
  A Custom Playlist in Vinyl Angel is a **channel federation**, not a flat list of individual song IDs. The property `channels: string[]` stores the names of the origin channels/playlists. When a custom playlist is streamed, all songs belonging to those member channels in `_1_static.db` become part of the stream.
* **Storage Layers**:
  1. **Frontend Store**: `customPlaylists: CustomPlaylist[]` in `useVinylStore.ts`, persisted in `localStorage` (`universe25-vinyl-angel-store`).
  2. **Backend Database**: Stored in `backend/data/projects/music_app/app_data/playlists.db`, table `playlists` (mapped to Tier `'playlists'` in `backend/data/projects/music_app/index.json`). In SQLite, the `channels` and `compatible_timeblocks` arrays are serialized as JSON strings.

### 4. How Custom Playlists Are Created, Updated, and Added To

1. **Creation**:
   * Initiated in `PlaylistManagerModal.tsx` or via `saveCustomPlaylist()` in `services/engine.ts`.
   * An ID is generated (`pl_${Date.now()}_${random}` if omitted).
   * Persisted to the backend:
     ```ts
     await executeOrder({
       project_id: projectId,
       tier: 'playlists',
       order: {
         action: 'upsert',
         key: pl.id,
         data: {
           name: pl.name,
           emoji: pl.emoji,
           description: pl.description,
           channels: JSON.stringify(pl.channels),
           compatible_timeblocks: JSON.stringify(pl.compatible_timeblocks),
           created_at: pl.created_at,
           updated_at: pl.updated_at,
         },
       },
     });
     ```
   * Added to store state: `addCustomPlaylist(saved)`.

2. **Updating**:
   * Form fields and selected channels are modified, then `saveCustomPlaylist()` is called with the existing `id`.
   * State is updated via `updateCustomPlaylist(saved)`.

3. **Adding the Playing Track's Origin Channel to an Existing Custom Playlist**:
   * For a playing track `currentTrack`, its source origin is `currentTrack.channel`.
   * To add this channel to a target custom playlist `targetPl`:
     ```ts
     if (!targetPl.channels.includes(currentTrack.channel)) {
       const updatedChannels = [...targetPl.channels, currentTrack.channel];
       const saved = await saveCustomPlaylist(targetProjectId, {
         ...targetPl,
         channels: updatedChannels,
       });
       updateCustomPlaylist(saved);
     }
     ```
   * Both `playlists.db` on the backend and `customPlaylists` in `useVinylStore` update immediately.

# Vinyl Angel — Complete Architectural & Gameplay Tab Knowledge Base

*Codex Location: `D:\My Drive\SandBox Projetcs\universe-25\src\apps\vinyl-angel`*  
*Target Project ID: `music_app` (`backend/data/projects/music_app`)*

---

## 1. System Overview & Multi-Tier Architecture

Vinyl Angel is an audio discovery, roulette curation, and harmonic rating application within Universe 25. It interfaces with an SQLite 5-Tier Data Engine exposed via HTTP API (`http://localhost:8080/api/v1/execute`).

### The Storage Tiers
1. **Tier 1 (`_1_static.db`)**: 
   - Static audio catalog.
   - Contains all scraped/ingested YouTube tracks (`id`, `title`, `channel`, `channel_id`, `duration`).
2. **Tier 2 (`_2_events.jsonl`)**:
   - Append-only event log recording every user rating action.
   - Event structure (`Tier2EventEntry`): `id`, `action` ('3+' | '4+' | '5+' | '6+' | '7+' | 'pass' | 'block'), `timestamp`, `timeblock`, `target_type` ('track' | 'channel'), `channel_id`, `channel_name`, `hazard_rank`.
3. **Tier 3 (`_3_state.db`)**:
   - Aggregated track and channel scoring state (`tier_3_data` table).
   - Tracks scores: `score_3_count` through `score_7_count` (stored as string arrays), `timeblock_arc0`..`arc4`, `unlock_date`, `hazard_rank`.
   - Also contains `channel_state` table for channel-level aggregate records.
4. **Tier 4 (`_4_display.db`)**:
   - Materialized display projections (`tier_4_data` table).
   - Precomputed `hazard_level`, `played`, `timeblock`, `unlock_date`, `rankCategory`, `hazard_rank`.
5. **Tier 5 (`_5_config.db`)**:
   - Player filter & configuration persistence (`tier_5_data` table, key: `'filter_settings'`).
   - Stores: `selectedChannel`, `excludedChannels`, `hazardCap`.
6. **Tier Playlists (`playlists.db`)**:
   - Custom thematic playlists created by the user (`playlists` table).
   - Stores: `id`, `name`, `emoji`, `description`, `channels` (JSON string array), `compatible_timeblocks` (JSON string array), `created_at`, `updated_at`.
7. **Tier Channel Metadata (`channel_meta.db` / `playlists.db`)**:
   - Origin channel curation statuses: `'raw' | 'cleaning' | 'approved'`.
8. **Blacklist & Unplayable Buffers**:
   - `blocked.db`: Permanently blacklisted songs.
   - `unavailable_videos.jsonl`: Unplayable YouTube videos (error codes 100, 101, 150) buffered before being pruned from Tier 1.

---

## 2. File Map & Responsibilities

| File Path | Role | Key Exports / Responsibilities |
|---|---|---|
| `VinylAngel.tsx` | Main Application Container | Tab navigation (`gameplay`, `gallery`, `playlists`, `ingestion`, `config`), theme switching, top currency counter (`Celestial Discs`, `Angel Roll Tickets`). |
| `types.ts` | TypeScript Domain Models | `CustomPlaylist`, `PlaylistItem`, `ChannelOriginItem`, `Tier2EventEntry`, `Tier3StateRecord`, `ScoreTier`, `VinylAction`, etc. |
| `store/useVinylStore.ts` | Zustand Global Store (Persisted) | Currencies (`discs`, `angelRollTickets`), shop purchases, settings, `customPlaylists`, `channelList`, `channelMetaMap`, `blockedSongIds`, inter-tab queued items. |
| `services/engine.ts` | Engine API & Mathematical Core | `fetchSampledTracks()`, `fetchCustomPlaylists()`, `saveCustomPlaylist()`, `deleteCustomPlaylist()`, `logRatingEvent()`, `getFilterConfig()`, `saveFilterConfig()`, `fetchChannelOrigins()`, `updateChannelStatus()`. |
| `components/VinylPlayer.tsx` | Gameplay Tab (Core Workstation) | YouTube iframe player, weighted roulette selection, filter controls (Include/Exclude/Hazard Cap), telemetry stats, harmonic rating deck. |
| `components/VinylPlaylists.tsx` | Playlists Tab | Displays Custom Playlists & Origin Channels, curation status toggles (`raw` -> `cleaning` -> `approved`), channel purging, playback trigger. |
| `components/PlaylistManagerModal.tsx` | Playlist Editor Modal | Create/edit Custom Playlist: name, emoji, description, member channel checklist, timeblock arcs. |
| `components/VinylGallery.tsx` | Gallery & Catalog Sync Tab | Full track leaderboard, search across Tier 1, manual ETL synchronization buttons, queue track to gameplay. |
| `components/VinylIngestion.tsx` | Song Ingestion Tab | Discover and curl YouTube playlists into Tier 1, SSE progress streaming, unplayable video review. |
| `components/VinylConfig.tsx` | Settings Tab | Theme selection, autoplay toggles, default pass score. |
| `components/VinylPipeline.tsx` | Pipeline Diagnostics | Direct diagnostic execution of ETL sync stages. |

---

## 3. Deep Dive: Gameplay Tab (`VinylPlayer.tsx`)

### Architecture & Lifecycle
1. **Mount & Filter Hydration**:
   - Reads persistent filter settings (`getFilterConfig`) from Tier 5 (`_5_config.db`).
   - Restores: `selectedChannel`, `excludedChannels`, `hazardCap`.
   - If queued item exists in `useVinylStore` (`queuedTrackForGameplay` or `queuedPlaylistForGameplay`), overrides active playback.
2. **Track Sampling (`loadData`)**:
   - Calls `fetchSampledTracks()` in `engine.ts`.
   - Filters out `blockedSongIds`.
   - Resolves active channel filter:
     - `ALL`: Samples across all channels.
     - `CUSTOM:<id>`: Resolves custom playlist channels array and samples from those channels.
     - `STATUS:approved | STATUS:cleaning | STATUS:raw`: Samples only channels with matching curation status.
     - `<channel_name>`: Samples songs exclusively from that single origin channel.
   - Applies `hazardCap` range filter.
   - Respects `excludedChannels` list.
3. **Roulette Track Selection (`selectWeightedTrack`)**:
   - $O(N)$ inverse-play-count weighting: $w = \frac{1}{\text{played} + 1}$.
   - Songs with 0 plays have highest probability; frequently played songs have lower probability.
4. **Buffer Maintenance**:
   - Local `playlist` array holds up to 50 sampled tracks.
   - When remaining unplayed tracks drop below 15, `replenishBufferIfNeeded()` triggers a background sampling request.
5. **YouTube Iframe Integration**:
   - Embeds `#vinyl-yt-player`.
   - Handlers for `onStateChange`:
     - Track Ends: If `autoplay` is enabled, automatically logs the track with default pass score and advances.
     - Errors (100, 101, 150): Appends to `unavailable_videos.jsonl`, excludes track, and spins to next track.

### Visual & Interactive Layout
1. **Telemetry & Filter Header (Top)**:
   - **Include Selector Dropdown**:
     - `ALL` (All Playlists)
     - `⭐ Custom Playlists` (`CUSTOM:<id>`)
     - `📁 Channel Status Groups` (`STATUS:approved`, `STATUS:cleaning`, `STATUS:raw`)
     - `📻 Individual Channels` (Alphabetical list of channels with track counts)
     - `⚙️ Manage Custom Playlists...`
   - **Hazard Drag Badge**: Real-time calculation showing how many 3.0 songs must be deleted/raised to gain +0.01 hazard average.
   - **Exclude Popover**: Multi-select checklist allowing the user to exclude specific Custom Playlists or individual channels.
   - **Hazard Cap Dropdown**: Filter by hazard tier (`7+`, `6+`, `3.2 to <6.0`, `<4.0`, `<3.2`, `All`).
   - **Metrics Pill Badges**: Pool count, session rated count, earned discs, offline outbox count, auto-sync batch counter (`X/15`).
2. **Left Column (Track & Video Deck)**:
   - Buffer position (`TRACK X / Y • Z in Pool`).
   - Song Title (`currentTrack.title`).
   - **Metadata Row**:
     - **Origin Channel / Playlist Name**: `{currentTrack.channel}`
     - **Track ID**: `ID: {currentTrack.id}`
     - **Play Count**: `Played: {getPlayedCount(currentTrack.id)}`
     - **Hazard Badge**: `HazardBadge` with score.
     - **Pick Chance**: Weighted probability percentage.
   - **16:9 YouTube Video Viewport**: `#vinyl-yt-player`.
3. **Right Column (Harmonic Rating Deck)**:
   - **Pin Button**: Locks ratings/ranks across tracks.
   - **Rating Target Toggle**:
     - `Single Song` (`'track'`): Logs rating to just `currentTrack.id`.
     - `All in Channel` (`'channel'`): Logs rating to all songs belonging to `currentTrack.channel`.
   - **Quick Action Row**:
     - `🥀 Cancel (3+)`: Quick log as 3+ and advance.
     - `🎲 Spin`: Skip to next roulette track without rating.
     - `✨ Pass (5+)`: Log with selected score / default score and advance.
   - **Hazard Rank Staging**: 3 (Base), 4 (Solid), 5 (Prime), 6 (Awaken), 7 (Crown).
   - **Score Tier Buttons**: 3+, 4+, 5+, 6+, 7+.
   - **Timeblock Arc Tags**: Arc Zero through Arc 04.
   - **Block Buttons**:
     - `Blacklist & Skip Now`: Immediate removal, block persistence to `blocked.db`, advance.
     - `Blacklist on Track End`: Flags song to be blocked once playback finishes.

---

## 4. Custom Playlists vs. Origin Playlists

### Key Distinction
- **Origin Playlist / Channel (`currentTrack.channel`)**:
  - The source YouTube playlist/channel that was ingested into Tier 1 (`_1_static.db`).
  - Represented as `channel` (string) on each track item.
- **Custom Playlist (`CustomPlaylist`)**:
  - A user-defined collection/federation of channels.
  - Interface:
    ```ts
    interface CustomPlaylist {
      id: string;                      // e.g. "pl_1712900000000_abcde"
      name: string;                    // e.g. "Cyberpunk Synthwave"
      emoji: string;                   // e.g. "⚡"
      description?: string;
      channels: string[];              // List of origin channel names
      compatible_timeblocks?: string[]; // Compatible timeblocks
      created_at: string;
      updated_at: string;
    }
    ```

   - Songs with 0 plays have highest probability; frequently played songs have lower probability.
4. **Buffer Maintenance**:
   - Local `playlist` array holds up to 50 sampled tracks.
   - When remaining unplayed tracks drop below 15, `replenishBufferIfNeeded()` triggers a background sampling request.
5. **YouTube Iframe Integration**:
   - Embeds `#vinyl-yt-player`.
   - Handlers for `onStateChange`:
     - Track Ends: If `autoplay` is enabled, automatically logs the track with default pass score and advances.
     - Errors (100, 101, 150): Appends to `unavailable_videos.jsonl`, excludes track, and spins to next track.

### Visual & Interactive Layout
1. **Telemetry & Filter Header (Top)**:
   - **Include Selector Dropdown**:
     - `ALL` (All Playlists)
     - `⭐ Custom Playlists` (`CUSTOM:<id>`)
     - `📁 Channel Status Groups` (`STATUS:approved`, `STATUS:cleaning`, `STATUS:raw`)
     - `📻 Individual Channels` (Alphabetical list of channels with track counts)
     - `⚙️ Manage Custom Playlists...`
   - **Hazard Drag Badge**: Real-time calculation showing how many 3.0 songs must be deleted/raised to gain +0.01 hazard average.
   - **Exclude Popover**: Multi-select checklist allowing the user to exclude specific Custom Playlists or individual channels.
   - **Hazard Cap Dropdown**: Filter by hazard tier (`7+`, `6+`, `3.2 to <6.0`, `<4.0`, `<3.2`, `All`).
   - **Metrics Pill Badges**: Pool count, session rated count, earned discs, offline outbox count, auto-sync batch counter (`X/15`).
2. **Left Column (Track & Video Deck)**:
   - Buffer position (`TRACK X / Y • Z in Pool`).
   - Song Title (`currentTrack.title`).
   - **Metadata Row**:
     - **Origin Channel / Playlist Name**: `{currentTrack.channel}`
     - **Track ID**: `ID: {currentTrack.id}`
     - **Play Count**: `Played: {getPlayedCount(currentTrack.id)}`
     - **Hazard Badge**: `HazardBadge` with score.
     - **Pick Chance**: Weighted probability percentage.
   - **16:9 YouTube Video Viewport**: `#vinyl-yt-player`.
3. **Right Column (Harmonic Rating Deck)**:
   - **Pin Button**: Locks ratings/ranks across tracks.
   - **Rating Target Toggle**:
     - `Single Song` (`'track'`): Logs rating to just `currentTrack.id`.
     - `All in Channel` (`'channel'`): Logs rating to all songs belonging to `currentTrack.channel`.
   - **Quick Action Row**:
     - `🥀 Cancel (3+)`: Quick log as 3+ and advance.
     - `🎲 Spin`: Skip to next roulette track without rating.
     - `✨ Pass (5+)`: Log with selected score / default score and advance.
   - **Hazard Rank Staging**: 3 (Base), 4 (Solid), 5 (Prime), 6 (Awaken), 7 (Crown).
   - **Score Tier Buttons**: 3+, 4+, 5+, 6+, 7+.
   - **Timeblock Arc Tags**: Arc Zero through Arc 04.
   - **Block Buttons**:
     - `Blacklist & Skip Now`: Immediate removal, block persistence to `blocked.db`, advance.
     - `Blacklist on Track End`: Flags song to be blocked once playback finishes.

---

## 4. Custom Playlists vs. Origin Playlists

### Key Distinction
- **Origin Playlist / Channel (`currentTrack.channel`)**:
  - The source YouTube playlist/channel that was ingested into Tier 1 (`_1_static.db`).
  - Represented as `channel` (string) on each track item.
- **Custom Playlist (`CustomPlaylist`)**:
  - A user-defined collection/federation of channels.
  - Interface:
    ```ts
    interface CustomPlaylist {
      id: string;                      // e.g. "pl_1712900000000_abcde"
      name: string;                    // e.g. "Cyberpunk Synthwave"
      emoji: string;                   // e.g. "⚡"
      description?: string;
      channels: string[];              // List of origin channel names
      compatible_timeblocks?: string[]; // Compatible timeblocks
      created_at: string;
      updated_at: string;
    }
    ```
  - **Core Mechanism**: A Custom Playlist groups multiple origin channels together. Streaming a custom playlist streams all songs belonging to any of its member channels.

### Persistence Mechanism for Custom Playlists
- **Database**: SQLite database `backend/data/projects/music_app/app_data/playlists.db`, table `playlists`.
- **API Call**: `saveCustomPlaylist(projectId, playlist)` in `services/engine.ts`.
- **Frontend Store**: `customPlaylists` in `useVinylStore.ts`, updated via `addCustomPlaylist(pl)` / `updateCustomPlaylist(pl)`.

---

## 5. Implementation Strategy: Adding the Playing Song's Playlist to an Existing Custom Playlist

When a song is currently playing in the Gameplay Tab:
1. The currently playing song's origin playlist/channel is `currentTrack.channel`.
2. Existing custom playlists are loaded in `useVinylStore` as `customPlaylists: CustomPlaylist[]`.
3. To add `currentTrack.channel` to an existing custom playlist `targetPl`:
   - Check if `targetPl.channels.includes(currentTrack.channel)`.
   - If not present:
     ```ts
     const updated = {
       ...targetPl,
       channels: [...targetPl.channels, currentTrack.channel],
     };
     await saveCustomPlaylist(targetProjectId, updated);
     updateCustomPlaylist(updated);
     ```
4. **UI Placement**:
   - Right next to `{currentTrack.channel}` in the track metadata line of `VinylPlayer.tsx` (line 2249), add an interactive button/popover: `[+ Add to Playlist]`.
   - The popover displays:
     - All custom playlists with `{pl.emoji} {pl.name}`.
     - Checkmark indicating if `currentTrack.channel` is already a member.
     - Click to toggle/add channel to that custom playlist.
     - Quick action to "+ Create New Playlist with this Channel" (opens `PlaylistManagerModal`).

# Implementation Plan: Add Playing Channel to Custom Playlist in Vinyl Angel

## 1. Architectural Overview and Data Flow

### Current Architecture
- In `D:\My Drive\SandBox Projetcs\universe-25\src\apps\vinyl-angel\components\VinylPlayer.tsx`, the currently active track is tracked via `currentTrack: PlaylistItem | null`.
- `currentTrack.channel` stores the origin channel name (e.g., "Lofi Girl", "Chillhop Music") of the currently playing track.
- Custom playlists are defined in `D:\My Drive\SandBox Projetcs\universe-25\src\apps\vinyl-angel\types.ts` as `CustomPlaylist`, where `channels: string[]` is an array of channel names.
- Custom playlists are persisted in SQLite `playlists.db` under tier `'playlists'` using `saveCustomPlaylist(projectId, playlist)` from `D:\My Drive\SandBox Projetcs\universe-25\src\apps\vinyl-angel\services\engine.ts`.
- In `D:\My Drive\SandBox Projetcs\universe-25\src\apps\vinyl-angel\store\useVinylStore.ts`, custom playlists are stored in Zustand state with `customPlaylists`, `updateCustomPlaylist(playlist)`, and `addCustomPlaylist(playlist)`.

### New Interaction Flow
1. **Trigger Action**: A dedicated "+ Playlist" button is positioned immediately adjacent to `{currentTrack.channel}` in the track metadata line below the title in `VinylPlayer.tsx`.
2. **Interactive Popover**: Clicking this button opens a celestial-themed popover positioned below the metadata bar.
3. **Membership Inspection**: The popover inspects all `customPlaylists` in `useVinylStore` and identifies whether `currentTrack.channel` is already a member of each playlist (`playlist.channels.includes(currentTrack.channel)`).
4. **Direct Add Action**:
   - For playlists where the channel is not yet present, a single click on the "+ Add" button appends `currentTrack.channel` to the playlist's `channels` array.
   - The updated playlist is persisted to SQLite via `saveCustomPlaylist(targetProjectId, updatedPlaylist)`.
   - The Zustand store is updated via `updateCustomPlaylist(saved)`.
   - A success toast is displayed using `showToast(...)`.
   - The popover updates reactively, changing the button to an "In Playlist" badge.
5. **Quick Create & Full Modal Integration**:
   - **Inline Quick Create**: An input box at the bottom allows typing a playlist name and hitting enter to immediately create a new custom playlist with `[currentTrack.channel]` pre-selected.
   - **Full Playlist Manager Modal**: A "Open in Playlist Manager" button opens `PlaylistManagerModal` pre-populated with `[currentTrack.channel]` in create mode, allowing the user to select an emoji, description, and timeblock constraints.

### Placement in Track Metadata Row

### Popover Layout and Structure
The popover dropdown follows the dark celestial aesthetic of Vinyl Angel:
- **Container**: `absolute left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 top-full mt-2 w-80 max-w-[90vw] bg-[#140f1c] border border-[#d4af37]/70 rounded-2xl shadow-2xl z-50 overflow-hidden flex flex-col text-left animate-in fade-in zoom-in-95 duration-150`

      - **Saving State**: When a playlist update is in flight, shows `<RefreshCw className="w-3 h-3 animate-spin text-[#ffd86b]" />`.
- **Inline Quick Create Section**:

- **Full Modal Launcher Footer**:

  - Launches `PlaylistManagerModal` with `initialSelectedChannels={[currentTrack.channel]}`.

## 3. State Management and Backend Persistence

### Store and Engine Imports
In `D:\My Drive\SandBox Projetcs\universe-25\src\apps\vinyl-angel\components\VinylPlayer.tsx`:
1. Import `saveCustomPlaylist` from `../services/engine`.
2. Destructure `addCustomPlaylist` and `updateCustomPlaylist` from `useVinylStore()`.
3. Import `Plus` and `Check` from `lucide-react`.

### Component State
```tsx
const [isAddToPlaylistOpen, setIsAddToPlaylistOpen] = useState<boolean>(false);
const [playlistSearchQuery, setPlaylistSearchQuery] = useState<string>('');
const [savingPlaylistId, setSavingPlaylistId] = useState<string | null>(null);
const [quickPlaylistName, setQuickPlaylistName] = useState<string>('');
const [isQuickCreating, setIsQuickCreating] = useState<boolean>(false);
const [preselectedChannelForModal, setPreselectedChannelForModal] = useState<string | null>(null);
const addToPlaylistRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
```

### Adding Channel to Existing Playlist Handler
```tsx
const handleAddChannelToPlaylist = async (targetPlaylist: CustomPlaylist) => {
  if (!currentTrack || !currentTrack.channel) return;
  const channelName = currentTrack.channel.trim();

  // Guard against duplicate addition
  if (targetPlaylist.channels.includes(channelName)) {
    showToast(`"${channelName}" is already in "${targetPlaylist.name}"`, 'info');
    return;
  }

  setSavingPlaylistId(targetPlaylist.id);
  try {
    const updatedChannels = [...targetPlaylist.channels, channelName];
    const updatedPlaylist: CustomPlaylist = {
      ...targetPlaylist,
      channels: updatedChannels,
      updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
    };

    // 1. Persist to SQLite playlists.db via engine
    const saved = await saveCustomPlaylist(targetProjectId, updatedPlaylist);

    // 2. Update Zustand store
    updateCustomPlaylist(saved);

    // 3. Provide toast confirmation
    showToast(`Added "${channelName}" to "${saved.name}"`, 'success');
  } catch (err: any) {
    console.error('Failed to add channel to playlist:', err);
    showToast(err.message || 'Failed to update playlist', 'error');
  } finally {
    setSavingPlaylistId(null);
  }
};
```

### Inline Quick Creation Handler
```tsx
const handleQuickCreatePlaylist = async (e: React.FormEvent) => {
  e.preventDefault();

const handleAddChannelToPlaylist = async (targetPlaylist: CustomPlaylist) => {
  if (!currentTrack || !currentTrack.channel) return;
  const channelName = currentTrack.channel.trim();

  // Guard against duplicate addition
  if (targetPlaylist.channels.includes(channelName)) {
    showToast(`"${channelName}" is already in "${targetPlaylist.name}"`, 'info');
    return;
  }

  setSavingPlaylistId(targetPlaylist.id);
  try {
    const updatedChannels = [...targetPlaylist.channels, channelName];
    const updatedPlaylist: CustomPlaylist = {
      ...targetPlaylist,
      channels: updatedChannels,
      updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
    };

    // 1. Persist to SQLite playlists.db via engine
    const saved = await saveCustomPlaylist(targetProjectId, updatedPlaylist);

    // 2. Update Zustand store
    updateCustomPlaylist(saved);

    // 3. Provide toast confirmation
    showToast(`Added "${channelName}" to "${saved.name}"`, 'success');
  } catch (err: any) {
    console.error('Failed to add channel to playlist:', err);
    showToast(err.message || 'Failed to update playlist', 'error');
  } finally {
    setSavingPlaylistId(null);
  }
};

const handleAddChannelToPlaylist = async (targetPlaylist: CustomPlaylist) => {
  if (!currentTrack || !currentTrack.channel) return;
  const channelName = currentTrack.channel.trim();

  // Guard against duplicate addition
  if (targetPlaylist.channels.includes(channelName)) {
    showToast(`"${channelName}" is already in "${targetPlaylist.name}"`, 'info');
    return;
  }

  setSavingPlaylistId(targetPlaylist.id);
  try {
    const updatedChannels = [...targetPlaylist.channels, channelName];
    const updatedPlaylist: CustomPlaylist = {
      ...targetPlaylist,
      channels: updatedChannels,
      updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
    };

    // 1. Persist to SQLite playlists.db via engine
    const saved = await saveCustomPlaylist(targetProjectId, updatedPlaylist);

    // 2. Update Zustand store
    updateCustomPlaylist(saved);

    // 3. Provide toast confirmation
    showToast(`Added "${channelName}" to "${saved.name}"`, 'success');
  } catch (err: any) {
    console.error('Failed to add channel to playlist:', err);
    showToast(err.message || 'Failed to update playlist', 'error');
  } finally {
    setSavingPlaylistId(null);
  }
};
```

# Plan: Add Playing Track's Origin Playlist/Channel to Custom Playlist in Vinyl Angel

## Context
In Vinyl Angel (`D:\My Drive\SandBox Projetcs\universe-25\src\apps\vinyl-angel`), audio streams can be filtered by origin channels (ingested YouTube playlists) or thematic **Custom Playlists** (federations of channels stored in `playlists.db`).
Currently in the Gameplay Tab (`VinylPlayer.tsx`), users can listen to a track, rate it, and view its origin channel (`currentTrack.channel`), but there is no direct action to add that playing track's origin channel to an existing custom playlist or create a new custom playlist around it without leaving gameplay to navigate to the Playlists Tab.

The intended outcome is to empower the Manager to seamlessly curate playing channels directly from the Gameplay workstation with a single click, persisting changes immediately to both the Zustand store and SQLite `playlists.db`.

---

## Recommended Implementation Approach

### 1. Interactive "+ Playlist" Popover in Track Metadata Row
In `VinylPlayer.tsx`, wrap the existing `{currentTrack.channel}` display (around line 2249) in a container with a compact trigger button:
- **Trigger**: `[+ Playlist ▾]` button adjacent to `{currentTrack.channel}`.
- **Visual Design**: Sleek celestial styling matching Vinyl Angel's theme (`bg-[#1a1424]`, border `#3d304f`, hover `#ffd86b`).
- **Popover Dropdown**:
  - Displays the active origin channel badge (`currentTrack.channel`).
  - Search filter input (if more than 4 custom playlists exist).
  - Scrollable list of user's custom playlists from `useVinylStore`:
    - Shows `{pl.emoji} {pl.name}` and member count.
    - **Already Member**: Displays a subtle green `✓ In Playlist` badge.
    - **Not Member**: Displays a `+ Add` button with hover glow and in-flight loading spinner.
  - **Inline Quick Create**: Simple text input + `+ Create` button to quickly forge a new custom playlist with `[currentTrack.channel]` pre-selected.
  - **Full Manager Launcher**: Link to open `PlaylistManagerModal` pre-populated with `[currentTrack.channel]`.

### 2. State & Engine Persistence Flow
When "+ Add" is clicked for a target playlist:
1. Verify `!targetPl.channels.includes(currentTrack.channel)`.
2. Construct updated playlist object:
   ```ts
   const updated = {
     ...targetPl,
     channels: [...targetPl.channels, currentTrack.channel],
     updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
   };
   ```
3. Call `saveCustomPlaylist(targetProjectId, updated)` from `services/engine.ts` (persists to `playlists.db`).
4. Update Zustand state via `updateCustomPlaylist(saved)` from `useVinylStore.ts`.
5. Display confirmation toast via `showToast(`Added "${currentTrack.channel}" to "${saved.name}"`, 'success')`.
6. Popover reactively reflects membership without closing, allowing multi-playlist assignment if desired.

### 3. Quick Create & Modal Pre-population
- **Inline Quick Create**: Calls `saveCustomPlaylist(targetProjectId, { name, emoji: '🎵', channels: [currentTrack.channel] })`, then `addCustomPlaylist(saved)`.
- **Full Modal Integration**: Extend `PlaylistManagerModal.tsx` to accept `initialSelectedChannels?: string[]`. When passed, modal defaults into `'edit'` mode with the current channel checked and ready for custom emoji/timeblock assignment.

---

## Critical Files to Modify

1. **`src/apps/vinyl-angel/components/VinylPlayer.tsx`**
   - Add state: `isAddToPlaylistOpen`, `savingPlaylistId`, `quickPlaylistName`, `isQuickCreating`, `playlistSearchQuery`, `preselectedChannelForModal`.
   - Add click-outside and escape-key event listeners for the popover ref.
   - Implement `handleAddChannelToPlaylist` and `handleQuickCreatePlaylist`.
   - Render the `[+ Playlist]` trigger button and popover dropdown next to `{currentTrack.channel}` in the track header.
   - Pass pre-selected channel into `PlaylistManagerModal`.

2. **`src/apps/vinyl-angel/components/PlaylistManagerModal.tsx`**
   - Extend `PlaylistManagerModalProps` with `initialSelectedChannels?: string[]`.
   - Add `useEffect` to pre-seed `selectedChannels` and start in `'edit'` mode when opened with `initialSelectedChannels`.

---

## Reused Functions & Utilities

- **`saveCustomPlaylist(projectId, playlist)`** (`src/apps/vinyl-angel/services/engine.ts:1806`):
  Persists custom playlists to SQLite `playlists.db` tier.
- **`updateCustomPlaylist` & `addCustomPlaylist`** (`src/apps/vinyl-angel/store/useVinylStore.ts:282-289`):
  Updates reactive Zustand store and browser localStorage.
- **`showToast(msg, type)`** (`src/apps/vinyl-angel/components/VinylPlayer.tsx:156`):
  Unified gameplay notification system.
- **`PlaylistManagerModal`** (`src/apps/vinyl-angel/components/PlaylistManagerModal.tsx`):
  Modal for comprehensive playlist configuration.

---

## Verification Plan

1. **Build & Type Check**:
   - Run TypeScript check or Vite build to confirm no type errors or regressions in `VinylPlayer.tsx` and `PlaylistManagerModal.tsx`.
2. **End-to-End Functional Verification**:
   - Open Vinyl Angel at `http://localhost:5173` (or active dev port).
   - In the Gameplay Tab, verify the `+ Playlist` button appears adjacent to the playing song's channel.
   - Click the button to inspect the popover:
     - Verify existing custom playlists are listed with correct membership status (`In Playlist` vs `+ Add`).
     - Click `+ Add` on a playlist: verify spinner, toast confirmation, and status switch to `In Playlist`.
     - Refresh the page and inspect `playlists.db` / Playlists Tab: verify the channel is preserved in that custom playlist.
   - Test inline quick create: type a name, hit create, verify playlist appears with the channel.
   - Test full modal trigger: click "Open Full Playlist Manager", verify `PlaylistManagerModal` opens in edit mode with the current channel selected.
   - Test edge cases: click outside to close popover, press Escape to close, verify UI behavior when no track is loaded.

# Plan: Add Playing Track's Origin Playlist/Channel to Custom Playlist in Vinyl Angel

## Context
In Vinyl Angel (`D:\My Drive\SandBox Projetcs\universe-25\src\apps\vinyl-angel`), audio streams can be filtered by origin channels (ingested YouTube playlists) or thematic **Custom Playlists** (federations of channels stored in `playlists.db`).
Currently in the Gameplay Tab (`VinylPlayer.tsx`), users can listen to a track, rate it, and view its origin channel (`currentTrack.channel`), but there is no direct action to add that playing track's origin channel to an existing custom playlist or create a new custom playlist around it without leaving gameplay to navigate to the Playlists Tab.

The intended outcome is to empower the Manager to seamlessly curate playing channels directly from the Gameplay workstation with a single click, persisting changes immediately to both the Zustand store and SQLite `playlists.db`.

---

## Recommended Implementation Approach

### 1. Interactive "+ Playlist" Popover in Track Metadata Row
In `VinylPlayer.tsx`, wrap the existing `{currentTrack.channel}` display (around line 2249) in a container with a compact trigger button:
- **Trigger**: `[+ Playlist ▾]` button adjacent to `{currentTrack.channel}`.
- **Visual Design**: Sleek celestial styling matching Vinyl Angel's theme (`bg-[#1a1424]`, border `#3d304f`, hover `#ffd86b`).
- **Popover Dropdown**:
  - Displays the active origin channel badge (`currentTrack.channel`).
  - Search filter input (if more than 4 custom playlists exist).
  - Scrollable list of user's custom playlists from `useVinylStore`:
    - Shows `{pl.emoji} {pl.name}` and member count.
    - **Already Member**: Displays a subtle green `✓ In Playlist` badge.
    - **Not Member**: Displays a `+ Add` button with hover glow and in-flight loading spinner.
  - **Inline Quick Create**: Simple text input + `+ Create` button to quickly forge a new custom playlist with `[currentTrack.channel]` pre-selected.
  - **Full Manager Launcher**: Link to open `PlaylistManagerModal` pre-populated with `[currentTrack.channel]`.

### 2. State & Engine Persistence Flow
When "+ Add" is clicked for a target playlist:
1. Verify `!targetPl.channels.includes(currentTrack.channel)`.
2. Construct updated playlist object:
   ```ts
   const updated = {
     ...targetPl,
     channels: [...targetPl.channels, currentTrack.channel],
     updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
   };
   ```
3. Call `saveCustomPlaylist(targetProjectId, updated)` from `services/engine.ts` (persists to `playlists.db`).
4. Update Zustand state via `updateCustomPlaylist(saved)` from `useVinylStore.ts`.
5. Display confirmation toast via `showToast(`Added "${currentTrack.channel}" to "${saved.name}"`, 'success')`.
6. Popover reactively reflects membership without closing, allowing multi-playlist assignment if desired.

### 3. Quick Create & Modal Pre-population
- **Inline Quick Create**: Calls `saveCustomPlaylist(targetProjectId, { name, emoji: '🎵', channels: [currentTrack.channel] })`, then `addCustomPlaylist(saved)`.
- **Full Modal Integration**: Extend `PlaylistManagerModal.tsx` to accept `initialSelectedChannels?: string[]`. When passed, modal defaults into `'edit'` mode with the current channel checked and ready for custom emoji/timeblock assignment.

---

## Critical Files to Modify

1. **`src/apps/vinyl-angel/components/VinylPlayer.tsx`**
   - Add state: `isAddToPlaylistOpen`, `savingPlaylistId`, `quickPlaylistName`, `isQuickCreating`, `playlistSearchQuery`, `preselectedChannelForModal`.
   - Add click-outside and escape-key event listeners for the popover ref.
   - Implement `handleAddChannelToPlaylist` and `handleQuickCreatePlaylist`.
   - Render the `[+ Playlist]` trigger button and popover dropdown next to `{currentTrack.channel}` in the track header.
   - Pass pre-selected channel into `PlaylistManagerModal`.

2. **`src/apps/vinyl-angel/components/PlaylistManagerModal.tsx`**
   - Extend `PlaylistManagerModalProps` with `initialSelectedChannels?: string[]`.
   - Add `useEffect` to pre-seed `selectedChannels` and start in `'edit'` mode when opened with `initialSelectedChannels`.

---

## Reused Functions & Utilities

- **`saveCustomPlaylist(projectId, playlist)`** (`src/apps/vinyl-angel/services/engine.ts:1806`):
  Persists custom playlists to SQLite `playlists.db` tier.
- **`updateCustomPlaylist` & `addCustomPlaylist`** (`src/apps/vinyl-angel/store/useVinylStore.ts:282-289`):
  Updates reactive Zustand store and browser localStorage.
- **`showToast(msg, type)`** (`src/apps/vinyl-angel/components/VinylPlayer.tsx:156`):
  Unified gameplay notification system.
- **`PlaylistManagerModal`** (`src/apps/vinyl-angel/components/PlaylistManagerModal.tsx`):
  Modal for comprehensive playlist configuration.

---

## Verification Plan

1. **Build & Type Check**:
   - Run TypeScript check or Vite build to confirm no type errors or regressions in `VinylPlayer.tsx` and `PlaylistManagerModal.tsx`.
2. **End-to-End Functional Verification**:
   - Open Vinyl Angel at `http://localhost:5173` (or active dev port).
   - In the Gameplay Tab, verify the `+ Playlist` button appears adjacent to the playing song's channel.
   - Click the button to inspect the popover:
     - Verify existing custom playlists are listed with correct membership status (`In Playlist` vs `+ Add`).
     - Click `+ Add` on a playlist: verify spinner, toast confirmation, and status switch to `In Playlist`.
     - Refresh the page and inspect `playlists.db` / Playlists Tab: verify the channel is preserved in that custom playlist.
   - Test inline quick create: type a name, hit create, verify playlist appears with the channel.
   - Test full modal trigger: click "Open Full Playlist Manager", verify `PlaylistManagerModal` opens in edit mode with the current channel selected.
   - Test edge cases: click outside to close popover, press Escape to close, verify UI behavior when no track is loaded.

content.thinking: The playlist management modal's visibility is controlled by a state variable. The modal receives project and channel data for context. Initial channel selection is based on a preselected value if one exists. On modal close, the visibility state resets and any preselected channel is cleared.

The plan is to implement an outside-click and Escape key handler to close a specific popover element. This handler will be associated with a reference. The initial step focuses on defining a function to detect clicks outside the referenced element, and setting the popover's open state to `false` when such an event occurs. This handler will be implemented as a `useEffect` hook.

Implemented an `Escape` key handler within the `useEffect` hook to close the playlist dialog, ensuring it's active only when the dialog is open. The event listeners for outside clicks and key presses are now conditionally added and removed based on the `isAddToPlaylistOpen` state, preventing memory leaks and unintended behavior.

The quick-create playlist functionality needs investigation, specifically focusing on its interaction with a target data structure that stores playlist information. It appears that the quick create playlist uses an asynchronous function to save to the playlist structure. It's essential to understand the data structure and how the created playlist integrates within the system's larger data flow.

Examining the "Add to Playlist" button's visual state transitions based on an internal state variable. The button's styling and text change, with an associated dropdown's visibility toggling based on the state. It seems the state variable directly controls the dropdown's display.

Analyzing a component displaying playlist information. The component includes a button to "Add to Custom Playlist" which toggles a dialog's visibility. There's also a display of the origin playlist and a search input that appears conditionally.

The origin playlist display truncates the playlist name if it exceeds the available space. The search input is displayed only when the number of custom playlists exceeds a threshold.

The playlist search input's visibility is tied to the custom playlists' count, suggesting a conditional rendering strategy to optimize UI. The search functionality filters a list of playlists based on user input, and the displayed list updates dynamically. It's observed that a "No matching playlists" message is displayed when the filtered list is empty, with the message text altering depending on if there are any existing custom playlists.

The component conditionally renders a message, either instructing the user to create a playlist or to try a different query, depending on the number of custom playlists. A list of filtered custom playlists is mapped to a set of display elements. Each playlist element includes indicators for membership status and saving state, along with truncated names.

Each custom playlist element's "Add" button's state is contingent on both a saving status and an "in playlist" indicator, presenting two distinct visual states. These visual states are updated based on internal state changes. The saving state is associated with a progress indicator. I will determine how the membership status is updated within the playlist data structure.

Investigating the quick playlist creation form. The form's submission handler likely triggers playlist creation via an asynchronous operation. Assessing how user input is validated and the creation action is managed through an internal state.

Manager, operations have concluded successfully.

### 1. Knowledge Base Repository
Per your directive, a comprehensive architecture and mechanics dossier for Vinyl Angel and the Gameplay Tab has been materialized at:
`D:\My Drive\SandBox Projetcs\ZZZ.md`

It documents:
- The 5-Tier Data Engine mapping (`_1_static.db` through `_5_config.db`, `playlists.db`, `blocked.db`).
- Component hierarchy, state machines, and lifecycle routines.
- Roulette track selection weighting ($w = \frac{1}{\text{played} + 1}$).
- Custom Playlist data contracts (`CustomPlaylist` channel federations).

---

### 2. Feature Implementation: Add Playing Channel to Custom Playlist

In the **Gameplay Tab** (`VinylPlayer.tsx`), you can now seamlessly curate and federate the origin playlist/channel whose song is currently playing into any existing or new custom playlist:

1. **Interactive Trigger**:
   - Directly adjacent to `{currentTrack.channel}` in the track header line under the title, a celestial `+ Playlist ▾` button is now active.
2. **Dynamic Membership Popover**:
   - Clicking opens a popover listing all user's custom playlists.
   - For playlists that already contain this channel, a badge displays `✓ In Playlist`.
   - For playlists where the channel is missing, clicking `+ Add` persists the update directly to SQLite `playlists.db` via `saveCustomPlaylist()` and updates the Zustand store reactively.
3. **Inline Quick Create**:

   - Clicking *"Open in Full Playlist Manager..."* launches `PlaylistManagerModal` pre-seeded with the playing channel in `'edit'` mode so you can assign custom emojis, descriptions, or timeblock arcs.

   - Outside click and `Escape` keyboard listeners auto-dismiss the popover.
   - TypeScript compilation and Vite production build verified with zero errors.

1	// path: src/App.tsx

3	import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react'
4	import { ThemeProvider } from './themes/ThemeProvider'
5	import { AppManager } from './core/AppManager'
6	import { useGlobalStore } from './store/useGlobalStore'
7	
8	export default function App() {
9	  const loadFromBackend = useGlobalStore((s) => s.loadFromBackend)
10	  const isOnline = useGlobalStore((s) => s.isOnline)
11	
12	  // Track previous online state so we can detect offline → online recovery
13	  const wasOnlineRef = useRef<boolean>(true)
14	
15	  // ── 1. Initial hydration on cold mount ────────────────────────────────────
16	  useEffect(() => {
17	    loadFromBackend()
18	  }, [loadFromBackend])
19	
20	  // ── 2. Periodic background re-hydration every 60 seconds ─────────────────
21	  // Keeps currency, inventory and vault in sync without requiring F5.
22	  useEffect(() => {
23	    const timer = setInterval(() => {
24	      loadFromBackend()
25	    }, 60_000)
26	    return () => clearInterval(timer)
27	  }, [loadFromBackend])
28	
29	  // ── 3. Tab-focus re-hydration via Page Visibility API ─────────────────────
30	  // Re-syncs the moment the user switches back to this tab.
31	  useEffect(() => {
32	    const handleVisibilityChange = () => {
33	      if (document.visibilityState === 'visible') {
34	        loadFromBackend()
35	      }
36	    }
37	    document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', handleVisibilityChange)
38	    return () => document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', handleVisibilityChange)
39	  }, [loadFromBackend])
40	
41	  // ── 4. Online-recovery re-hydration ───────────────────────────────────────
42	  // When the backend flips from offline → online, immediately re-hydrate
43	  // to pick up any mutations that happened while we were disconnected.
44	  useEffect(() => {
45	    const wasOffline = !wasOnlineRef.current
46	    if (wasOffline && isOnline) {
47	      loadFromBackend()
48	    }
49	    wasOnlineRef.current = isOnline
50	  }, [isOnline, loadFromBackend])
51	
52	  return (
53	    <ThemeProvider>
54	      <AppManager />
55	    </ThemeProvider>
56	  )
57	}
